claim_label: Positive-Pressure Confinement of Superelastic NiTi Wire Bundle
claim_text_original: Positive-pressure confinement of a superelastic NiTi wire bundle remains open.
claim_text_normalized: Direct external application of positive fluid or membrane confinement pressure to radially compress a superelastic NiTi wire bundle to modulate stiffness.
why_potentially_novel: At mentor proposal and early V002, actively varied positive confinement pressure (P3) was hypothesized to establish a new class of variable-stiffness beam mechanics distinct from fixed-preload cables.
search_conducted: MP1-V002 targeted threat audit across subsea cables, wire ropes, and pressurized bundles.

strongest_prior_art_threat.paper_title: Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable
strongest_prior_art_threat.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2017-Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable.pdf
strongest_prior_art_threat.what_source_actually_proves: Models external radial contact pressure (0.2 MPa) acting on a multi-component dynamic cable under cyclic bending with Coulomb friction and stick-slip transitions.
strongest_prior_art_threat.what_source_does_not_prove: Applies a constant external radial pressure rather than actively modulating pressure as a variable stiffness control parameter on a NiTi bundle.

source_records.paper_title: Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable
source_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2017-Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable.pdf
source_records.what_source_actually_proves: Radial confinement pressure directly shifts inter-wire contact pressure and bending stick-slip thresholds in cables.
source_records.what_source_does_not_prove: Does not use NiTi or actively vary pressure during operation.

source_records.what_source_actually_proves: Derives layer-by-layer radial contact pressure Pi and demonstrates that radial pressure dictates interlayer friction and curvature-dependent bending rigidity.
source_records.what_source_does_not_prove: Pressure is passive/helix-induced, not externally controlled.

source_records.paper_title: A new mechanical model of short wire ropes: Theory and experimental validation
source_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2025-A new mechanical model of short wire ropes.pdf
source_records.what_source_actually_proves: Shear-deformable beam model with internal contact friction; incremental equilibrium equations naturally accommodate transverse loading.
source_records.what_source_does_not_prove: Does not study actively pressurized NiTi bundles.

claim_before: Positive-pressure confinement of a superelastic NiTi wire bundle creates an unaddressed class of mechanics.
claim_after: Positive pressure is an experimental boundary condition; existing incremental contact formulations accommodate p(t) without new physical laws.
reason_for_change: Astra critique G02 and remediation worker W05 proved that incremental contact-friction equations (f_t <= mu * f_n(p)) naturally accept time-varying pressure p(t).
scientific_consequence: P3 is demoted from a 'mechanics principle' to an 'experimental control protocol'. Novelty cannot be claimed based on pressure adjustability alone.
feasibility_impact: Requires careful independent calibration of pressure-to-contact-force transmission (membrane and arching effects).
pivot_relevance: Key correction in Stage 3 preventing false claim of mechanics novelty based on active pressure.
historical_interpretation: Treated as candidate mechanics novelty in early V002 (S05/S06). Remediated in Stage 3 (S12) into a boundary condition for testing existing models.
superseded_interpretation: Belief that varying pressure dynamically (P3) constituted a distinct mechanical theory separate from fixed preload (P2) or passive preload (P1).
corrected_interpretation: P1, P2, P3 are loading protocols, not distinct mechanics laws; contact equations naturally accept p(t).
